context: Alfred's minibus taxi: the weekly passenger totals are grouped, and the takings are estimated from the centre of each group.

params.why: the fare per passenger (distance times rate per km) must be a whole number of rand

params.name: total
params.let: sum([cs[i] * mids[i] for i in range(6)])

stem: Alfred runs a minibus taxi. Over {=n} weeks he counted the passengers he carried each week and sorted the weekly totals into groups, where $x$ is the number of passengers in a week: ${=lo[0]}<x\leq{=lo[1]}$ in {=cs[0]} weeks; ${=lo[1]}<x\leq{=lo[2]}$ in {=cs[1]} weeks; ${=lo[2]}<x\leq{=lo[3]}$ in {=cs[2]} weeks; ${=lo[3]}<x\leq{=lo[4]}$ in {=cs[3]} weeks; ${=lo[4]}<x\leq{=lo[5]}$ in {=cs[4]} weeks; ${=lo[5]}<x\leq{=lo[6]}$ in {=cs[5]} weeks. Estimate how much money Alfred made over these {=n} weeks by treating every week in a group as having the number of passengers at the centre of that group. Assume that every passenger travelled an average of {=d} $\text{km}$ and that Alfred charged R{=fixed(rc / 100, 2)} per $\text{km}$. Give your answer in rand.
solution: Treat every week in a group as having the number of passengers at the centre of its group. The centres of the six groups are {=mids[0]}, {=mids[1]}, {=mids[2]}, {=mids[3]}, {=mids[4]} and {=mids[5]}.

Multiply each count of weeks by the centre of its group and add, to estimate the total number of passengers: ${=cs[0]}({=mids[0]})+{=cs[1]}({=mids[1]})+{=cs[2]}({=mids[2]})+{=cs[3]}({=mids[3]})+{=cs[4]}({=mids[4]})+{=cs[5]}({=mids[5]})={=total}$ passengers.
Each passenger travelled {=d} $\text{km}$ at R{=fixed(rc / 100, 2)} per $\text{km}$, so each passenger paid ${=d}\times{=fixed(rc / 100, 2)}={=per}$ rand.
The estimated takings are ${=total}\times{=per}={=takings}$, so Alfred made about R{=takings}.
notes: Mirrors book Ex 10.4 Q3(b) and (e): total passengers from count x centre, then x km x rate. The histogram is replaced by the same grouped data written in the stem (intervals of the form a < x <= b, width 100, six groups, counts are numbers of weeks). Counts are drawn as 6 distinct values from 2..11 so a group is never empty. d is even and the rate is a multiple of R0.50, so the fare per passenger is always a whole number of rand and the answer is a whole number (about 150 000 to 1 200 000, the book's own is 588 000). The Rand is kept as in the book. Only the estimate under the centre-of-group rule is asked for, and the stem states that rule, so a solver cannot take the exact total.
